failures.resolution: At the user request, only huge-file was rerun with 21 accepted paired samples. The report uses that successful rerun, not the initial partial samples.

boundaries: Configurations ran in separate sequential batches, each paired with the same Go executable. Cross-configuration differences are descriptive rather than one randomized multi-runtime trial.
CLI timings include process startup and use warm filesystem caches. Each workload has three warmup pairs and 21 measured pairs.
Warm checker timings include fresh program construction, binding and complete semantic checking in retained processes. Input decoding and forced collections before/after each iteration are excluded.
CLI validates normalized diagnostics/exit status and emitted language bytes, excluding tsbuildinfo. Checker validates source graph hashes and diagnostic counts, not full diagnostic text.
NativeAOT targets use their toolchain defaults with no host-native instruction-set override; CoreCLR has tiering enabled and runtime-default dynamic PGO. No processor count override is used.
Satori uses the requested custom ILC and aotsdk, which include compiler, CoreLib and runtime changes beyond the GC. Its timings do not isolate a collector-only effect.
Ordinary desktop background activity remains recorded. Input-contaminated checker batches were excluded and rerun.
The 256 MiB settings are not an equal enforced budget across Go and the .NET collectors; Satori limit semantics are not asserted here.
The original Server GC large-file access violation is retained separately from the successful requested rerun.
